speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble eating and your belly is swollen. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, does the vomit look like it has white, curd-like lumps?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the tenderness on abdominal exam is concerning. Given the feeding difficulties, distension, and irritability, have you noticed any blood in your stools or if they are passing gas at all?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
No fever, vomiting, or diarrhea is noted, and the baby had an uncomplicated birth. Given the progressive abdominal distension, feeding refusal, and tenderness, do you see any visible veins on your baby's belly or a bulge at the umbilicus?
